answer: Challenge-Bound Query Routing: each agent identity must answer a fresh, randomly generated task whose correct output depends on a secret seed delivered once, then discarded. Answers are checked against a one-way hash commitment, so copying a prior response fails. An attacker pays a unique solve per identity, scaling cost linearly with bots. A zephyr of random seeds rotates hourly. Idle agents on the tundra still owe one solve per epoch. Each valid solve mints a small opal credit, making mass registration economically negative.
